title: I Enforced the Orchard Picking Quota on the Volunteer Lead Who Filled Two Crates

parts.text: I checked in for one crate at 9:08 a.m. and lead Fran was already on crate two under a volunteer badge. The tree sign said: ONE CRATE PER U-PICK. VOLUNTEERS SAME QUOTA. I was fifty-three, u-pick, holding a single punch card. Fran kept filling. "Leads are the orchard." I photographed the two crates, the sign, and her badge. Then I logged a double. At 9:16 the farm stand asked why Fran's badge was on two crates. I asked once, then I documented twice. The second photo is for the person who will say they never saw the first.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The farm stand can see two crates under Fran's volunteer badge against the one-crate sign.

social.video_title: The volunteer lead filled two crates on a one-crate quota — Part 1/2
social.description: Orchard, a punch card, and a second crate. I logged the double. Would you have photographed the badge?

parts.text: Fran called it seconds until the stand asked for the log. I printed the double, the photo, and the sign. Crate two went to the stand. Fran picked one and told volunteers seconds were always about optics. Optics is a word leads use when a second crate exists. Quota now has a second line: LEADS ARE NOT TWO. I keep one punch. Fran stands. The trees finally look like a u-pick, not a pantry. The room sounds like a room again, not a title. Petty is a word people use when their name is on the ticket.

social.description: Double log, crate to the stand, and a second line. Was seconds ever a badge?
